plain_definition: Number of heatwaves a year. A heatwave is 3 or more days in a row that are unusually hot for that place.
caveat: 'Unusually hot' means the top 10% of 1981-2010 summer days for that place, so the temperature bar differs between towns.

plain_definition: Number of days a year that fall inside a heatwave (3 or more unusually hot days in a row).
caveat: 'Unusually hot' means the top 10% of 1981-2010 summer days for that place, so the temperature bar differs between towns.

plain_definition: Length of the longest heatwave of the year, in days. Zero means the year had no heatwave.
caveat: One long hot spell can dominate a year, so single years jump around a lot.

plain_definition: The day of the year the first heatwave starts. A smaller number means heatwaves arrive earlier.
caveat: Years with no heatwave have no date and are left out, so this trend uses fewer years.

plain_definition: The highest daytime temperature reached in the year.
caveat: NASA values are averages over a roughly 50 km square, so peaks read lower than a city weather station.

plain_definition: Number of nights a year that stay unusually warm for that place, the kind that make sleep difficult.
caveat: 'Unusually warm' means the top 10% of 1981-2010 summer nights for that place.

plain_definition: Number of days a year with summer-like warmth: a 5-day average temperature of 15 °C or more.
caveat: 15 °C is a fixed bar, so colder northern towns have short 'summers' by this measure.

plain_definition: The day of the year autumn chill arrives: the first time after 1 July the 5-day average drops below 10 °C.
caveat: A single early cold snap can pull the date forward in any one year.

plain_definition: The day of the year of the first autumn frost: the first night after 1 August at 0 °C or below.
caveat: Mild years with no frost before 31 December have no date and are left out. Local frost hollows are missed by 50 km data.

plain_definition: The most rain that fell in a single day in the year.
caveat: NASA values are averages over a roughly 50 km square, so a local downpour reads lower than a rain gauge under it.

plain_definition: Number of days a year with 10 mm of rain or more, a properly wet day.
caveat: Rain swings a lot from one year to the next, so a trend needs to be large before it can be told apart from chance.

plain_definition: The longest run of days in a row with under 1 mm of rain, in June to August.
caveat: One long dry spell can dominate a year (56 days in London in 2018), so single years jump around a lot.

plain_definition: Total rain from December to February. The winter is named after the year its January falls in.
caveat: The first winter is 1981-82, so 1981 has no value. Rain swings a lot from one year to the next.

plain_definition: Average sunlight energy reaching the ground each day in June to August. A higher number means sunnier, less cloudy summers.
